Cc: Tom Singh <tom.singh@mededge.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on pricing exhibit caps/floors

Hi Kim,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Our procurement team has reviewed the draft Order Form and flagged an ambiguity in Exhibit B around the "annualized floor" and the "safety cap" language. Specifically: are usage true-ups measured against raw token counts (per monthly invoices) or the annualized aggregated commit? The way the current wording reads we could end up double-counting buffered credits when a quarterly spike triggers the cap.

Attached is a redline annotated by our finance team (MedEdge_pricing_redlines.pdf) with two proposed edits:
- Option A: clarify that floors are evaluated on annualized committed units, excluding any one-time burst credits.
- Option B: add explicit language excluding prefix/KV cache credits from the floor calculation.

We want to avoid a retroactive billing dispute. Can you confirm Redwood's interpretation and whether you can agree to either Option A or B? If not, we need a short mediation note so our CFO can sign off.

Thanks,
Anna Morales
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedEdge Health

[Attachment: MedEdge_pricing_redlines.pdf (PDF)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna.morales@mededge.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on pricing exhibit caps/floors

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. I read this with Connor (ops) and Laura (billing) and below is our proposed mediation summary for the Order Form:

1) Measurement basis: Floors and caps will be evaluated on the customer's annualized committed units as stated in Exhibit B. The annualized commit is the baseline for true-up calculations.

2) Exclusions: One-time promotional/burst credits and explicit operational prefix/KV cache credits will be excluded from the floor calculation. We will add a short definitional paragraph in Exhibit B to capture these exclusions.

3) Invoice-level adjustments: Monthly invoices remain the operational billing document; any true-up related to the annualized floor/cap will be reconciled on the following quarter's invoice with a clear line item called "Annualization True-Up."

4) Guardrail: To avoid disputes, both parties agree to a carry-forward dispute window of 90 days from the true-up invoice date.

Action items:
- Connor to produce a one-page markup showing the exact Exhibit B paragraph to insert (Connor: ETA EOD Wed).
- Laura to prepare an example invoice illustrating the Annualization True-Up line item (Laura: ETA Thu morning).
- I will confirm with Legal whether the wording needs a clause-level concession or can be an ops-level clarifying paragraph.

I've attached Connor's early sketch (KIYER_annotated_exhibit_B.xlsx) — it's preliminary. If this summary looks right to you, we can circulate a redline and get both legal and procurement approvals.

Kim Park
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: KIYER_annotated_exhibit_B.xlsx (Excel)]

Anna / Kim — quick operational note from my side after mapping a few spike scenarios:

- Using the annualized commit as baseline keeps billing predictable and avoids monthly noise from transient spikes. That's our preference.
- On exclusions: we can explicitly exclude both burst credits and cached-token discounts, but we should add an examples table (two rows) so accounting knows what to exclude.
- For systems: we'll add a tag to any one-off credits so they can't be auto-included in the annualization pipeline. That requires a brief ops ticket (I can own).

Proposed language snippet for Exhibit B (draft):
"Annualization baseline shall mean the customer's committed units over the 12-month period specified in the Order Form. For the avoidance of doubt, temporary promotional credits, burst credits, and explicitly labeled cache or prefix credits will be excluded from the baseline computation."

If Anna agrees I will convert this into the tracked-change redline and drop it back into the thread.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Platform Operations (Redwood)
